process_defect_fixed_in_this_cycle.what: apply_session_penalties() in priority.py crashed with KeyError('score_inputs') the moment AUT-PROP-002 (a hand-filed row with no `score_inputs` field, since only graph-derived rows carry one) had a non-empty `blocked_evidence` set on it -- the function assumes any entry with a non-null score also carries score_inputs. Root cause was this cycle's own edit: `blocked_evidence` is semantically for a BLOCKED item awaiting an observation, not for a SUPERSEDED item being closed out, and using it for the latter was the wrong field regardless of the crash. Fixed by moving the explanatory text to a new `superseded_note` field and leaving `blocked_evidence: null`. Not filed as a ledger process_defect because it was caught and fixed within this same cycle, before any commit landed on a broken re-score -- but worth naming here per CLAUDE.md §4's root-cause-with-evidence rule rather than silently self-correcting.
